key_concepts: Factors affecting reaction rates include temperature, catalyst, concentration, and surface
Adding heat or increasing temperature increases reaction rate
Removing heat or lowering temperature decreases reaction rate
Adding a catalyst increases reaction rate
Increasing concentration increases reaction rate while diluting decreases it
Breaking a substance into smaller pieces increases surface area and reaction rate
Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings
Exothermic reactions release heat to the surroundings
Endothermic processes make surroundings cooler while exothermic processes make surrounding
Both endothermic and exothermic reactions form new substances and involve bond breaking an
Melting ice and cooking egg are endothermic examples
Burning wood and firecrackers are exothermic examples
